cards.title: Polarization measurement state

source_refs.value: Eq. (7), TeX label measurement directions as Kets

cards.role: Defines the transmitted polarization projector used in every Born probability.
assumptions: angles are converted from degrees to radians before trigonometric evaluation
derivation_steps: The paper supplies the ket in Eq. (7).
Its norm is sin(theta)^2+cos(theta)^2=1.
The plus-outcome measurement operator is the outer product of the normalized ket.
cards.numerical_form: q(theta) = [sin(theta), cos(theta)] in the [H,V] basis; projector = outer(q, q.conj()).

checks.reason: The ket is transcribed from frozen Eq. (7).

cards.title: Fitted two-photon source state
cards.role: Defines the pure component of the fitted source model.
derivation_steps: The two counter-propagating source amplitudes occupy orthogonal |HV> and |VH> basis states.
Their squared amplitudes sum to w+(1-w)=1.
At w=1/2 and xi=pi the state is the singlet.
cards.numerical_form: psi = [0, sqrt(w), exp(1j*xi)*sqrt(1-w), 0] in the [HH,HV,VH,VV] basis.

checks.reason: The state is transcribed from frozen Eq. (18).
The orthogonal component probabilities sum identically to one.

cards.title: Isotropic-noise density matrix
cards.role: Defines the fitted mixed state whose probabilities form every generated model curve.
assumptions: I_4 is the identity on the two-qubit Hilbert space
derivation_steps: A normalized rank-one projector has trace one.
The isotropic component I_4/4 also has trace one.
The eigenvalues are (1+3v)/4 along |Psi> and (1-v)/4 in each orthogonal direction.
For 0<=v<=1 the matrix is Hermitian, positive semidefinite, and trace one.

checks.reason: The density operator is transcribed from frozen Eq. (20).
The analytic eigenvalues sum to one.
The analytic eigenvalues are non-negative over the stated parameter domain.

cards.title: Density-matrix Born probability
cards.role: Evaluates each of the three plus-plus probabilities for the fitted mixed state.
assumptions: Alice and Bob use local rank-one projectors
derivation_steps: The joint plus-plus ket is |alpha> tensor |beta>.
Born's rule gives <alpha,beta|rho|alpha,beta>.
For xi=pi the pure-state amplitude is sqrt(w) sin(alpha) cos(beta) - sqrt(1-w) cos(alpha) sin(beta).
The normalized white-noise term contributes exactly (1-v)/4.
For w=1/2 this reduces to v sin(alpha-beta)^2/2+(1-v)/4.

checks.reason: The singlet form is transcribed from Eq. (9); the trace form is its standard density-matrix extension used by Eq. (20).
A positive unit-trace density matrix evaluated on a projector yields a probability in [0,1].

cards.title: Wigner value
cards.latex: \mathcal W=P_{++}^{\hat a\hat b'}+P_{++}^{\hat b\hat c'}-P_{++}^{\hat a\hat c'}
cards.role: Combines the three generated probability curves into the main plotted observable.
assumptions: the three probabilities use the same density matrix and target scan coordinate
derivation_steps: The set-theoretic identities in Eqs. (1)-(3) give W=p3+p6 for the LHV model.
Non-negative hidden-set probabilities imply W>=0.
The same linear combination is evaluated with quantum Born probabilities for each target.
cards.numerical_form: W = p_ab + p_bc - p_ac, evaluated pointwise on the common angle grid.

checks.reason: The linear combination is transcribed from frozen Eq. (5).
Substitution of Eqs. (1)-(3) reduces W to p3+p6.

cards.title: Singlet analytic Wigner limits
cards.role: Provides model-independent analytic checks for symmetric and asymmetric target geometries.

symbols.Delta_xy: relative angle between the two indicated projectors

derivation_steps: Insert the singlet Born probability into the Wigner combination.
For symmetric spacings (phi,phi,2phi), W=sin(phi)^2-sin(2phi)^2/2.
At phi=pi/6 this equals -1/8.
For asymmetric separations (pi/12,pi/12,pi/4), W=(1-sqrt(3))/4.

checks.reason: The formula and angle choices are transcribed from Eqs. (9)-(13).
Symbolic substitution at pi/6 returns exactly -1/8.

cards.title: Fidelity to the singlet
cards.role: Checks the fitted state against the paper's reported singlet fidelities.
assumptions: the pure comparison target in the results paragraph is the singlet
derivation_steps: For a pure target, Eq. (21) reduces to the expectation value of rho.
The squared overlap between the singlet and |Psi(w,pi)> is 1/2+sqrt(w(1-w)).
The isotropic component contributes 1/4.
Rounded w and v values can shift the recomputed fidelity by a few 1e-3 relative to the reported fitted value.

checks.reason: The pure-target trace formula is transcribed from Eq. (21); the surrounding text identifies the singlet comparison.
w=0.5 and v=0.98 give F=0.985 exactly, matching the paper.
